t:
(a) 
Paragraph (1) of section 394 of the Communications Act of 1934 is amended by striking out “and” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands”.
 
    (b) 
Paragraph (4) of such section is amended by inserting “and, in the case of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, means the High Commissioner thereof” before the period at the end thereof.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to definitions in the Communications Act of 1934, extending them to cover U.S. territories and the Trust Territory's High Commissioner. The tempting reading is that bringing territorial governments into the definitions implies coordination with outside entities, but the text itself creates no consultation, hearing, comment, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No outside party is brought into any federal decision here.
fable.s: in the case of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, means the High Commissioner thereof

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the text of the Communications Act of 1934, specifically updating the list of territories and defining the relevant official for the Trust Territory. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards, or hearings. It is purely a legislative drafting amendment.
qwen_block.s: (a) Paragraph (1) of section 394 of the Communications Act of 1934 is amended by striking out “and” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands”. (b) Paragraph (4) of such section is amended by inserting “and, in the case of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, means the High Commissioner thereof” before the period at the end thereof.

opus.w: This section is a technical amendment. It adds the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands to a definition in section 394, and names the High Commissioner for the Trust Territory. It creates no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty, or right to sue. The territories and High Commissioner appear only as defined terms in what is a grant program, and grant eligibility is not participation in a federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that adding territories and the High Commissioner to section 394 brings outside governments into a federal process, so it counts as participation. That doesn't hold up. The amendment only changes definitions. Section 394 sets definitions for the Communications Act's educational broadcasting facilities grant program. At most, being covered lets an entity apply for grants, and grant applications are excluded.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the definitions within the Communications Act to include specific territories and officials. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in federal decision-making. The changes are purely definitional and do not involve any procedural requirement for engaging with non-federal entities.
qwen_chat.s: Paragraph (1) of section 394 of the Communications Act of 1934 is amended by striking out “and” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting before the period at the end thereof “, the Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending definitions to include territories or officials implies some form of consultation or participation with those entities. However, this section merely updates statutory definitions and jurisdictional scope. It does not create any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from outside parties (such as the High Commissioner or residents of the territories) before a federal decision is made. The changes are purely definitional and administrative.
